title: Bechtle and IQM Awarded DLR QCI Contract to Supply Superconducting Cloud Resources - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
IT service provider Bechtle and superconducting quantum hardware manufacturer IQM Quantum Computers (NASDAQ: IQMX) have been awarded a public contract by the German Aerospace Center’s Quantum Computing Initiative (DLR QCI) to supply cloud-based quantum computing resources and hybrid infrastructure.

Under a multi-year framework agreement running through June 2027, Bechtle will provide DLR QCI research and application teams with managed access to IQM’s production-grade superconducting quantum processors via the IQM Resonance™ cloud platform. The contract expands DLR QCI’s existing hardware portfolio—which already includes ion-trap, neutral-atom, photonic, and NV-center systems—by adding European-built superconducting hardware for application benchmarking in materials science, aerospace engineering, mobility, and security.

To support hybrid quantum-classical algorithms and high-performance computing (HPC) workflows, the contract includes a dedicated classical server stationed directly alongside IQM’s quantum hardware at its Munich data center. Bechtle’s IT System House Bonn is responsible for setting up platform governance, account management, and operational user support for DLR QCI researchers.

The award expands upon the commercial partnership established between Bechtle and IQM in 2024, reinforcing national data sovereignty requirements for Germany’s federally funded research programs under the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space.
